0.label: head_face_and_upper_rim
0.description: The top of the drawn tray: a calm face with lidded eyes at the head of the rim, between ribbed blocks, with the start of the knotted-serpent compartments on either side.
0.iconography: The ojú ọpọ́n (Ẹ̀ṣù) face that orients the tray.

1.label: knotted_serpent
1.description: In the lower-left rim compartment, a snake with a dotted body looped into a knot around a lozenge, its head with an eye turned back toward the face.
1.iconography: A serpent tied in a knot — the snake as guardian and as the binding, self-returning coil of the ouroboros family. Paired with #2 on the other side.

2.label: knotted_serpent
2.description: The mirror of #1 in the lower-right compartment: dotted snake looped round a lozenge, head with an eye.
2.iconography: See #1: a pair of knotted serpents flanking the foot of the tray.

panel.title: Drawn round Ifá tray: face at the head, knotted serpents around the rim
panel.object_type: pen-and-ink survey drawing of a round opon Ifá
panel.summary: A Frobenius survey drawing of a round Ifá tray: a hatched working field, a calm face at the head of the rim, and compartments of knotted dotted serpents separated by ribbed blocks.

register_readings.reading: Knotted serpents on both sides of the foot; more on the flanks (undetected), each between ribbed blocks.

panel.composition: A ring with one face and repeated serpent compartments, mirrored about the vertical axis.
panel.narrative: An Ifá tray guarded by serpents: every compartment but the head holds a snake tied in a knot. It is the clearest pairing of Ẹ̀ṣù and the serpent in the collection — the messenger and the coiled guardian — and one of the strongest serpent / ouroboros images the project is tracking.
panel.hypotheses: Neutral for 'chronicle'. The serpent compartments are counted units around the rim (about six to eight), a possible structure to compare with other trays.
uncertainties: Side compartments are cropped by the sheet edge and not boxed.
The knotted forms could be read as lizards with looped tails.
